sources.title: PlayStation cancels live-service shooter Fairgames
sources.text: Haven Games to "shift focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation" PlayStation has cancelled Fairgames, the live-service shooter previously in development at its Montreal-based subsidiary Haven Studios. In a statement to Bloomberg , PlayStation said Haven Studios will "shift focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." No jobs have been cut due to the cancellation. According to an email reviewed by Bloomberg, executives Sean Decker and John Doyle informed employees that a recent Fairgames playtest did not meet expectations. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," they said. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." Haven Studios' debut game was announced in 2023, initially scheduled for release last year, and later delayed to Spring 2026. Jade Raymond founded Haven Studios in 2021, and PlayStation Studios acquired the studio in 2022. Following Raymond's departure in May 2025 , executive producer Marie-Eve Danis and Pierre-François Sapinski were appointed co-studio heads. PlayStation started focusing on the live-service market in 2022 by acquiring Bungie for $3.6 billion . Former Sony Interactive Entertainment head Jim Ryan said the company aimed to launch more than ten live-service games by 2026 . Sony reduced the value of its acquisition by $765 million in the 2025/26 fiscal year after Destiny 2 and Marathon underperformed. Earlier this year, Bungie laid off 292 employees and ended development on Destiny 2. Following the game's final update, Bungie announced plans to reinstate vaulted campaigns , raids, and destinations to restore player trust. One of Sony’s most publicised live-service failures was Concord in 2024 , which was withdrawn from sale two weeks after release. Sony subsequently closed its developer Firewalk Studios , along with Neon Koi. Koi. In 2025, Sony cancelled two unannounced live service titles from Bend Studio and Bluepoint Games. The following year, Sony closed Bluepoint, resulting in 70 job losses . Sony Interactive CEO Hideaki Nishino previously said he wanted to "revitalise" live-service projects through a combination of first- and third-party content following its string of failures. "We believe that live service games are content that attracts users on a global level, so we want to continue to revitalise the market through both first-party and third-party content," Nishino said. "We are not only focusing on promoting new releases, but also considering what we can do with older titles in the medium to long term." He continued: "With live service games, it's important to continuously provide something. The genre itself is relatively new, and I think many people are trying various things, so we also want to continue to take on challenges within that context."

sources.title: Sony cancels live-service shooter Fairgames
sources.text: Fairgames is PlayStation’s latest cancellation as it steps back from many of its live service efforts.﻿ Fairgames is PlayStation’s latest cancellation as it steps back from many of its live service efforts.﻿ Sony has canceled Fairgames , a heist game announced in 2023 , according to Bloomberg . Fairgames had once been part of Sony’s big planned push for PlayStation live service games, but the company ended up canceling some planned live service titles, including in the God of War and The Last of Us franchises, and it shut down Concord shortly after its failed launch . The Fairgames cancellation won’t result in job cuts, and developer Haven Studios will now support other PlayStation studios, Bloomberg reports. The game was canceled following a recent test where “player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” according to part of an executive memo published by Bloomberg , which also cited “challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre.” Sony acquired Haven Studios in 2022 . Sony’s live service efforts have seen some success with Helldivers 2 , which is also available on Xbox . Bungie’s Marathon , which launched this year, has had a rough start , but today the studio showed off some new features coming in a December update , including a new co-op PvE roguelite mode and a PvP deathmatch mode. Sony is also working on a live service Horizon spinoff, but recently rebooted it .

sources.title: Sony cancels another live service game ahead of release, but at least there won't be any layoffs this time
sources.text: Fairgames was revealed in 2023, but nothing more was ever seen of it. A Bloomberg report says Fairgames, a PvP heist shooter announced by Haven Studios and Sony in 2023 , has been cancelled. In something of a surprising twist, a PlayStation rep told the site there will be no layoffs as a result of the cancellation, as Haven will "shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." While it was announced three years ago, work on Fairgames appears to have started even further back, in 2021. Just a couple months after her high-profile split with Google Stadia , Assassin's Creed co-creator Jade Raymond announced the formation of Haven Studios , which was "working on an unannounced new IP for PlayStation." In 2022, right around the time former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan was talking about launching 12 live service games by 2025, Sony acquired the studio outright; a year after that, Fairplay was revealed to the world. But things have not gone smoothly since then. Helldivers 2 was a massive hit, but seven of those planned games were cancelled before release . Of the remaining games, one was Marathon , which endures but has not lived up to expectations, and another was Concord , one of the most famously disastrous game launches in years, which was taken offline less than two weeks after it launched, never to return. A live-service spinoff of the Horizon series, Hunters Gathering, was also reportedly rebooted after negative feedback from playtests . A partial accounting of canned multiplayer projects: The Concord catastrophe in particular seemed to shake Sony, which began reversing its live service strategy just a few months later. Fairgames itself looked to be in trouble in 2025 when Raymond departed Haven , reportedly after an external playtest left PlayStation leadership "concerned about how the game was received and its progress." The Bloomberg report says a more recent large-scale playtest produced similar results. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email sent to Haven Studios employees. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." The one bright spot to the cancellation is that no jobs will be cut because of it: A Sony rep told Bloomberg that Haven "will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: PlayStation's embattled shooter Fairgames has finally been cancelled, a new report says, as live service push withers away
sources.text: After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames. The Haven-developed co-op heist shooter has been cancelled, with the silver lining that the studio is not closing down or laying off staff. According to a new Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest. Sony told staff on Tuesday of the playtest's poor reception and of its decision to end development. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PvP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." A PlayStation spokesperson later confirmed that developers at Haven will now support other teams within the PlayStation Studios group, as they continue to "explore new creative opportunities". Fairgames was initially announced in 2023 as one of several in-development live service games, as part of an initiative by former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan to create more than a dozen games that generate recurring revenue . Most of those titles were cancelled before they were even revealed, and those that made it out, such as Concord, flopped severely . Even Sony darling Guerrilla Games seemingly can't make it work, with recent reports saying the studio's Horizon Hunters Gathering - initially envisioned as a live service spin on the robo dinosaur series - will now shift into a more traditional co-op structure without live service elements. That's assuming the team can show a revamped version of the game to executives by December. The news of Fairgames' cancellation isn't surprising. The game has had a tumultuous development journey ever since its reveal. Initially set for release in 2025, the game was soon pushed back to 2026 , following the departure of studio founder Jade Raymond . Though Sony later reiterated its commitment to its remaining in-development live service titles , Fairgames was never shown to the public again. That same year, game director Daniel Drapeau left Haven - another key departure suggesting the game had difficulties and might not see release. Throughout that time, Fairgames has reportedly been reworked multiple times, with a plan for it to be re-revealed under a new name. That name is believed to be Break In, linked to a trademark Sony filed in May , but with the project cancelled, we may never know if that was the case.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake sells in huge numbers, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been a huge success for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game ever, shifting more than 5.2 million copies in four days. Nintendo announced the sales result this morning in a press release, specifying that the record relates only to Nintendo-published games. But since Nintendo's games are the most popular Switch 2 games, the fastest-selling-ever title presumably holds. It's an incredible result for a game that's been received with enormous enthusiasm. Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time five golden stars in Eurogamer's review , saying: "Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve." We've also already seen a jump in US Switch 2 sales because of the game's release. So much for not launching in November near GTA 6 , eh? This level of success begs the question of whether Nintendo would consider remaking more beloved old Zelda games - or Nintendo games - to replicate this nostalgia-driven effect. Are there other Zelda games that have the pull of Ocarina of Time that haven't been remade or remastered already in some capacity? If you're inspired to pick the game up because of this, or already have it, know that we've got a whole proverbial library shelf of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides to help you through the game.

sources.title: How to complete the Frog side quest in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake
sources.text: The Fabulous Five Froggish Tenors need five songs played to them in OoT, which unlocks a new minigame. The Frogs in The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time are found in the Zora River, and need songs played to them to complete their side quest. Referring to themselves as the Fabulous Five Froggish Tenors, Link's goal is to play five songs to them that they want to hear, which then unlocks a new minigame that you can play. If you can complete the frog song minigame, that then grants you a new piece of heart, a very valuable commodity. If you want to know how to complete this side quest, I'll take you through a full walkthrough below and what you need to know about the frogs and their love of music. To find the Five Froggish Tenors and start this side quest, you need to go to Zora River, which is accessed via the Northeast edge of Hyrule Field. Halfway along this route, on the North side, you'll find a small alcove with five pillars in it. This is where the Frogs are waiting. Simply interact with them like any NPC to begin the quest. You need to play several specific songs for the Frogs on your Ocarina for the chance to unlock the minigame, each one of which grants the players rupees as a reward. You need to play the following songs (in any order): As a bonus, players can also play the Song of Storms, learned from the Kakariko Windmill as an adult as part of a quest to learn the Lenses of Truth in Zelda Ocarina of Time . This isn't necessary to unlock the quest, but playing the Song of Storms for the frogs will grant you an additional piece of heart. Once all five necessary songs have been played, you can unlock the Frog Song minigame. Unfortunately, OoT doesn't actually explain how to control it, which can make it tricky. Here's how it works: Input it correctly, and you'll be awarded another piece of heart! sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is selling way more physical copies than digital in Japan
sources.text: Roughly two-thirds of its sales were physical The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is selling more physical copies and digital copies in Japan, and by some margin to boot. Japanese magazine Famitsu 's latest sales chart numbers are in, with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time unsurprisingly at the top. According to its data, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Nintendo Switch 2 sold 537,041 physical copies at Japanese retailers. Earlier this week, Nintendo confirmed that the latest Zelda release had sold over 5.2 million copies within four days of launch, making it "the highest global sales for any Nintendo-published Nintendo Switch 2 game in its first four days." Nintendo specified that 810,000 of these copies were sold in Japan. This means the Ocarina of Time remake sold around 272,959 digital copies in the region, roughly a third of the game's total sales in the region. With Sony 's decision to end physical disc production in 2028, and Rockstar releasing a ton of copies of GTA 6 today that feature nothing more than a code in a box that will activate in a week's time, there's been a lot of debate around physical game releases as of late. However, it's clear there's still a market out there for them, even if it is shrinking. Granted, Zelda's fortunes may have been helped by the fancy physical boxed copy that the game launched with, but even so, two-thirds of the game's sales in the region are certainly significant. sources.title: Resident Evil Requiem wins four Golden Joystick Awards, including Ultimate and Console GOTY
sources.text: Capcom receives seven awards, including Studio of the Year and recognition for Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword The 44th Golden Joystick Awards took place last night, with Resident Evil Requiem winning four awards including Ultimate Game of the Year and Console Game of the Year. The ninth instalment in the franchise also received Best Game Trailer, in addition to Angela Sant'Albano winning Best Lead Performer for her role as Grace Ashcroft. Capcom received seven awards, including Studio of the Year, Best Audio Design for Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and Best Supporting Performer for Grace Saif’s role as Diana in Pragmata. AdHoc's Dispatch earned Best Storytelling and Best Soundtrack. Meccha Chameleon was recognised as Best Indie Game (self-published), Best Multiplayer Game, Streamer’s Choice, and Developer’s Choice. Elsewhere, Remedy received Best Visual Design for Control Resonant, Unknown Worlds' Subnautica 2 won Best Early Access Game, Pearl Abyss's Crimson Desert was named PC Game of the Year, and House House's Big Walk received Critics' Choice. sources.title: Resident Evil Requiem wins Ultimate Game of the Year at the Golden Joystick Awards 2026
sources.text: Resident Evil Requiem has walked away with the biggest prize of the night at the Golden Joystick Awards 2026 , claiming the title of Ultimate Game of the Year. Competition was fierce for this year's main award, with Resident Evil Requiem coming out at the top of the pile of 12 of this year's biggest games. Those included the massive launches of Crimson Desert and Phantom Blade Zero, blockbuster 007: First Light, surprise hits like Control Resonant and Pragmata, and late additions in the form of Star Wars: Galactic Racer and The Blood of Dawnwalker. Also nominated were Big Walk, Dispatch, Forza Horizon 6, and Pokemon Pokopia. The win capped off a big night for Resident Evil Requiem, which came away from this year's ceremony with four awards; Best Game Trailer for its 'Evil Always Has a Name' promo, Best Lead Performer for Grace Ashcroft actress Angela Sant'Albano, and Console Game of the Year. That might have made it the outright winner, were it not for an astonishing challenge from a very different game - two player-voted and two jury-voted awards for Meccha Chameleon saw the hide-and-seek sensation tie Resi's four wins. But Resident Evil Requiem has still walked away with the biggest prize, and depending on exactly how you count each award, may have pipped Meccha Chameleon to the title, thanks to a Studio of the Year award for Capcom - though with that shared with fellow winners Pragmata and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, perhaps that's a total of just 4.33 awards for Resi. Requiem has been a long-time frontrunner for this year's GOTY conversations. With the spectre of GTA 6 just over the horizon it will likely struggle to complete the sweep of the Big 5 awards, but it's certainly shrugged off the recency bias that can always affect awards shows - when it launched back in February, we described it as "a loving pastiche of the series' greatest hits," and "a seesaw of terror and wonder." sources.title: The Witcher 4 and The Witcher 3 Remastered secure wins for CD Projekt Red at the Golden Joystick Awards
sources.text: CD Projekt Red was one of the bigger winners at the Golden Joystick Awards 2026 , as both The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 claimed prizes. The 2015 RPG classic took home the prize for the Best Remake/Remaster, thanks to its acclaimed re-release from earlier this year. That extends The Witcher 3's run as the most-awarded game in Golden Joysticks history, having previously won 11 titles between 2013 and 2016, including Studio of the Year prizes for CDPR and a Best Performance award for Geralt actor Doug Cockle. That total now stands at 12 awards, and with Songs of the Past on the way next year, it could still grow. Later in the night, The Witcher 4 took home the award for the Most Wanted Game. It's in some auspicious company on that front - in 2024 and 2025, it was GTA 6 that claimed that prize, but in recent memory it's also been won by the likes of Elden Ring, Tears of the Kingdom, and God of War: Ragnarok. However, no studio is better-equipped to take up that mantle than CD Projekt Red, which has already won this particular prize four times in the past - twice for The Witcher 3 in 2013 and 2014, and another two times for Cyberpunk 2077 in 2018 and 2019. That last one didn't work out quite as smoothly as CDPR might have hoped in the short term, but no doubt they'll be happy to have added another prize to their collection. Elsewhere, the biggest winners were Resident Evil Requiem, which took home four prizes, including Ultimate Game of the Year and Best Lead Performer for Grace actress Angela Sant'Albano (with a fifth for Studio of the Year Capcom ), and viral sensation Meccha Chameleon, which tied Resi thanks to two player-voted and two jury-voted awards. sources.title: Why wasn't GTA 6 at the Golden Joystick Awards?
sources.text: You'll have to wait a little while for Leonidas The Golden Joystick Awards 2026 have drawn to an end, but one of this year's biggest games was entirely absent: GTA 6 . If you were watching the ceremony wondering where Rockstar might have been, the short answer is that GTA 6 was not eligible for entry at this year's show. To be nominated in one of the main categories, a title had to release between November 1, 2025 and September 25, 2026. For the main prize of Ultimate Game of the Year, that window was extended to October 25, and for jury-voted prizes, games are eligible up until the show itself, November 11. That means that games like Dispatch, which launched late last year, or Phantom Blade Zero, which only just released, were eligible to be included in the 2026 show. But GTA 6, which is set to release next week, arrives eight days after the eligibility window closed. It was technically eligible for the title of Most Wanted game, but given that Rockstar won that particular award in 2024 and 2025, and that the wait is so nearly over, GTA 6 wasn't nominated in that category. Adding to the potential confusion is the fact that GTA 6 is eligible for The Game Awards. Those take place on December 10, several weeks after launch, and the fact that they're jury-voted rather than public-voted means that any jurors with review access might have had copies of the game for some time before that show. The rest of the major awards shows - namely the DICE, GDC, and BAFTA ceremonies - take place at the start of 2027, so GTA 6 will likely be a major contender there. GTA 6 will be eligible for the 2027 Golden Joystick Awards, where I'd also expect it to pick up several prizes. That means that it will be able to complete the clean sweep of the Big 5 shows - repeating the feats of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Baldur's Gate 3 - but it won't do so in the 2026/7 season. sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Crimson Desert wins 'PC Game of the Year' at the 2026 Golden Joystick Awards
sources.text: Resident Evil Requiem and Meccha Chameleon were the night's other big winners. There was some fun conversation here at PC Gamer recently about the anachronistic name of The Golden Joystick Awards, which are put on by PC Gamer's publisher. Who even uses a joystick anymore? Flight sim diehards, fighting game enthusiasts, and not many others. So why is it called that? Joysticks , really? Simply put, the name reflects the age of the awards, which debuted in 1983, making it the longest-running publicly-voted videogame awards show of all time, according to Wikipedia. Back in those days, joysticks were it, and trust me, they weren't the sweet pieces of hardware we have access to now. But we loved 'em! And we used them to play games like the Golden Joysticks' first-ever game of the year, Jetpac. It was a banger! Here we are, 43 years later, and much has changed: From a tiny ceremony handing out five trophies, the Golden Joysticks have grown to become one of the biggest videogame awards events of the year, watched by millions of people around the world on just about every streaming platform you can name. Yet that name, the Golden Joystick Awards , remains. Frankly, I'm glad about that. A little bit of reliability in this world is good for everyone. Which leads me to the point: The 44 th annual Golden Joystick Awards has now concluded, and the top gong , as my UK compatriots like to say for some reason—the Ultimate Game of the Year award, for the rest of us—has gone to Resident Evil Requiem , Capcom's latest tale of zombie-fueled bad news. Can't really argue with that call: PC Gamer's Elie Gould gave Resident Evil Requiem a whopping 92% score in their review , saying it "feels like you're playing a highlight reel of the best moments in the series." Requiem claimed three other wins on the night: Console Game of the Year, Best Game Trailer, and Best Lead Performer for Angela Sant'Albano's turn as Grace Ashcroft. Crimson Desert won for PC Game of the Year, which surprises me a bit given that it's also on consoles and pretty much the same experience. We liked that one too: Not quite as enthusiastically, but it still earned an enviable 80% review score . "Vast and obtuse in a way that is going to frustrate some and exhilarate others," as reviewer Mollie Taylor put it: "A fascinating journey, even when the destination isn't all that." Multiplayer hide-and-seek game Meccha Chameleon was the night's other big winner, taking home four awards for Best Multiplayer Game, Best Indie Game (self-published), the Steamers' Choice Award, and Developer's Choice Award. Dispatch won twice, for Best Storytelling and Best Soundtrack, and The Witcher also sort of claimed two wins as well: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered took the trophy for Best Remake/Remaster, while The Witcher 4 won for Most Wanted Game. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. So there you have it, 44 years down and hopefully many more to come—all of them bearing that glorious golden name. Here's your full list of 2026 Golden Joystick Awards winners: 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill. sources.text: Lançamentos de games em NOVEMBRO de 2026 - Calendário VOXL Além do aguardado GTA 6, novembro traz remake de Ocarina of Time e mais de 30 jogos. Confira as estreias do mês. Crédito: Voxl A fabricante de acessórios para eletrônicos Logitech oficializou, nesta quarta-feira (10), um novo benefício curioso. A partir de agora, funcionários da companhia podem tirar um dia de folga remunerada apenas para se dedicar a videogames . A campanha se chama Gaming Time Off, ou GTO , e foi confirmada em um comunicado oficial pela própria CEO da companhia, Hanneke Faber. De forma bem humorada, ela mesma reconhece que o timing da revelação tem a ver com o lançamento de Grand Theft Auto 6 e com o provável número grande de ausências de pessoas no próprio emprego durante o primeiro dia de disponibilidade do game. “Para os funcionários da Logi que planejam uma viagem a Vice City, não é mais preciso pegar a “gripe GTA” — basta tirar o seu GTO”, brinca a executiva no LinkedIn . O GTO estará disponível para todos os funcionários da Logitech , mas o texto oficial não explica se há limitações sobre quando a folga pode ser tirada ou quantas pessoas da equipe conseguem sair no mesmo dia, por exemplo. De acordo com a fabricante, famosa por produtos como mouses, teclados e fones de ouvido, a folga é uma forma de reconhecer os “ benefícios cognitivos e profissionais ” da prática de jogos digitais. “É hora de deixar de lado o estereótipo de que jogar videogame é perda de tempo. Como uma empresa que desenvolve produtos tanto para o trabalho quanto para o lazer, observamos diariamente como o engajamento em uma dessas esferas favorece o desempenho na outra ”, complementa a CEO. O jogo da Rockstar sai em 19 de novembro deste ano e deve ser um dos maiores fenômenos recentes da indústria. O título já bateu recordes de pré-venda nos consoles e pode ser baixado antecipadamente por quem já fez a compra. sources.title: Logitech dará dia de folga para funcionários jogarem videogame; Brasil está incluído
sources.text: A Logitech anunciou uma iniciativa que promete agradar aos funcionários que gostam de videogames: um dia de folga dedicado exclusivamente aos jogos . Batizado de Logi Game Day , o benefício será oferecido aos colaboradores da empresa, incluindo os profissionais que trabalham no Brasil. A iniciativa marca o primeiro dia dedicado aos games em toda a história da Logitech e tem como objetivo reconhecer o papel dos videogames no desenvolvimento de habilidades que também podem ser utilizadas no ambiente profissional. O evento acontecerá em 19 de novembro de 2026 , mesma data prevista para o lançamento de GTA 6 . Segundo a empresa, a decisão está relacionada a pesquisas sobre a influência dos games no desenvolvimento de competências profissionais. Um levantamento da Logitech, chamado Ctrl Tomorrow , apontou que 81% dos jogadores entrevistados acreditam que os videogames contribuem para a autoconfiança, ajudam a reduzir a ansiedade e estão associados a um melhor desempenho nas atividades cotidianas. Outro estudo citado pela fabricante revelou que 98,8% dos profissionais responsáveis por decisões de tecnologia da informação consultados acreditam que habilidades desenvolvidas nos jogos podem ser aplicadas ao trabalho. Entre essas competências estão pensamento estratégico, resolução de problemas complexos e capacidade de atuar sob pressão. Os resultados representam percepções dos participantes das pesquisas e não comprovam, isoladamente, que jogar videogame melhora o desempenho profissional. “Chegou a hora de deixar para trás o estereótipo de que jogar é perda de tempo”, afirmou Hanneke Faber, CEO da Logitech. Para celebrar a iniciativa, a Logitech G realizará uma transmissão ao vivo diretamente de sua sede em San Jose, nos Estados Unidos, no dia 19 de novembro. O evento será apresentado por Robin Piispanen, gerente-geral da Logitech G e ex-jogador profissional. Segundo Piispanen, experiências em jogos como GTA 6 , Call of Duty e Forza podem estimular a colaboração e a resolução de problemas. A diretora de Recursos Humanos da Logitech, Elaine Laird, também destacou que reservar um período para atividades de lazer pode ajudar os colaboradores a retornar ao trabalho com novas perspectivas. Com o Logi Game Day, a fabricante passa a incorporar os videogames à sua política de benefícios, defendendo que jogar pode representar não apenas entretenimento, mas também uma oportunidade de desenvolver habilidades e fortalecer a integração entre equipes. sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Laid-off Id Software devs form employee-owned studio Hidden Horses
sources.text: Developer is launching a Kickstarter campaign to fund its first project, FPS shooter Danger Pay A group of Id Software developers affected by Xbox's mass layoffs have formed an independent, employee-owned studio called Hidden Horses. The studio includes more than 20 former Id Software developers, artists, and designers, and aims to provide staff with an ownership stake in their work. "We're creating a studio where the developers share in its success and have a commitment to it beyond just another job," said co-founder and executive producer Andrew Willis. "I think that when people have a stake in something’s success, they are more committed to it." Hidden Horses wants to utilise this structure to "empower individual developers while maintaining the focused decision-making necessary to build ambitious games." The developer is launching a Kickstarter campaign to fund its first project, the single-player FPS Danger Pay. Funds will support "the typical things needed to start a business and finance game development, including licenses, hardware, and healthcare." The initial fundraising goal will reflect the timeline and costs of the first project. "What excites me about this particular venture is we're taking the two kinds of risk that I was holding before," co-founder and rendering programmer Regan Carver said in a video documenting the studio's founding . "One was, can we succeed, which was a given because we were an established company. We had money coming in. We were making good stuff. And the other was, does the company care about me? For a while, that was true, and then it stopped." "Whereas with this venture, it's like trading one for the other. We know we all care about each other, but all we have to do now is succeed. I've done the former. It didn't work out. I'm ready to do the latter, being able to do what we want and talk through what our ideas are." In July, approximately 136 Id employees were laid off. The developer maintained it still had " the crew we need to build the games and tech we're known for ," despite concerns about its ability to maintain its proprietary game engines with half a team. "The team today is about the same size we were when making Doom (2016)," the developer said in a statement. "We have always had a flat studio where everyone is a maker, and we will remain true to that philosophy moving forward." "We are focused on supporting each other and the team members impacted. We're going to keep building the great games and tech that have defined us for the past 35 years."

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Former id Software developers form their own employee-owned shooter studio in the wake of Microsoft's mass layoffs
sources.text: Hidden Horses, co-founded by "approximately 20" former id devs, is planning a Kickstarter campaign to help fund its first project. As part of its July 2026 wave of Xbox job cuts, Microsoft laid off a reported 136 developers from id Software, a studio whose name is synonymous with expertise in shooter design and engineering. Today, "approximately 20" of those former id developers announced the formation of Hidden Horses, an employee-owned game studio boasting "over 250 collective years" of game dev experience between its co-founders. "This team has spent years building games together, and we realized that what made that experience special wasn't just the projects we worked on; it was the people we worked with," Hidden Horses engine programmer and co-founder Dustin Land said in a press release . "Hidden Horses is an opportunity to keep that team together, build something of our own, and create the kind of old school shooters that we think people want more of." On its website , the studio says it was formed as a democratically governed, developer-owned company so it can prioritize "long-term health over short-term growth, longevity over quarterly returns, and innovative gameplay over shady monetization"—for the sake of its games, and the studio staff creating them. "We're creating a studio where the developers share in its success and have a commitment to it beyond just another job," said co-founder and executive producer Andrew Willis, "I think that when people have a stake in something’s success, they are more committed to it.” The studio is planning to launch a Kickstarter campaign to support the development of its first planned game: a singleplayer arena shooter called Danger Pay, in which players will participate in a televised ultraviolent game show inspired by works like The Running Man (the 1987 movie, not the 2025 one) and 1990's Smash TV—a game that, I've just now learned, got a novella adaptation in 1992 . So. Now I get to have that knowledge bouncing around. "We've had the privilege of spending our careers making games for incredible communities of players," said Johnmichael Quinlin, studio co-founder and tools programmer. "Now we have the chance to build something new together, and we're excited to invite those players along for the journey from the very beginning." If you want to stay posted on what Hidden Horses is up to, you can follow the studio on its Bluesky account . Leveraging the brainworms from a youth spent in World of Warcraft to write for sites like Waypoint, Polygon, and Fanbyte, Lincoln spent three years freelancing for PC Gamer before joining on as a full-time News Writer in 2024, bringing an expertise in Caves of Qud bird diplomacy, getting sons killed in Crusader Kings, and hitting dinosaurs with hammers in Monster Hunter. sources.name: Video Games Chronicle
sources.title: A group of developers laid off from id Software have formed new studio Hidden Horses
sources.text: The studio is Kickstarting its first game, an FPS called Danger Pay A team of developers who were recently laid off from id Software have formed a new studio, and plan to make a new FPS. Hidden Horses is an employee-owned studio consisting of more than 20 former id Software staff, and aims to “pursue fun and creativity in our games, unencumbered by short-term thinking or chasing market trends”. “As a group of developers who’ve dedicated their careers to making games, we believe this structure allows us to create the kind of company that values long-term health over short-term growth, longevity over quarterly returns, and innovative gameplay over shady monetization,” a statement from the studio reads. The studio has launched a short documentary video explaining how they were all laid off from id Software, how the layoffs affected them, and how they got together to form Hidden Horses. “Okay, you’ve got all these people that do this amazing thing at a high level, that really cannot be replicated, and they’re all out of a job now,” producer Andrew Willis said in the video. “You have all these people on the consumer side that love the games, want more of it, and want more of it than has even been produced in the past. “So, if the money’s out there to buy the stuff that we make, and the people who make that stuff are now free to make more of it, I just thought we should, we could do this. The demand is there, the supply side is there. There’s no reason that we can’t put a company together to continue this on. “Especially as I saw the [ Doom: The Dark Ages ] Revelations DLC critical reviews and player reviews roll in, of just loving it, a lot of them saying it’s the best entry in the whole Doom trilogy from 2016 on, I just became more and more convinced if we put together a company full of these veterans that hold all this immense institutional knowledge, I think the fans would want to buy what they would have to make.” The new studio has turned to Kickstarter in an attempt to get funding for its first game, a first-person shooter called Danger Pay set in a deadly gameshow, with inspiration taken from The Running Man and Smash TV. “Unlike a lot of potential startups, having a team that has already worked together for a decade, you already have those connections,” technical artist Todd Boyce said in the video. “You already all know what each other’s capabilities are. and you already know how to make a game together. To put together a team like the team that this tragedy has kind of spurned, is almost a one in a million opportunity that just doesn’t happen. “Having the ability to inject your own creativity into a project gives you so much more ownership. And this is an opportunity for an entire team to do that on a new project of their own creation. And that is the most exciting thing I could possibly imagine.”

stories.title: GTA 6 Was Almost Refused a Rating in South Korea Due to 'Genital Nudity'
stories.summary: GTA 6 was almost too much for South Korean ratings board GCRB, who struggled to agree whether the game should be approved or not. The board cited “out of context genital nudity” as the sticking point.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: GTA 6 Was Almost Refused a Rating in South Korea Due to 'Genital Nudity'
sources.text: GTA 6 was almost too much for South Korean ratings board GCRB, who struggled to agree whether the game should be approved or not. The board cited “out of context genital nudity” as the sticking point. Rockstar sent an application for a South Korean rating on September 1. The initial vote, held on September 10, ended in a tie, with three votes for classification refusal and three for an Adults Only rating. InvenGlobal acquired the meeting minutes from the voting sessions, where some board members argued for classification refusal over in-game nudity. When voting resulted in a tie, they chose to postpone the decision while awaiting a playable build of the game. A GTA 6 build was delivered to the committee on September 28 and an initial revisit of the board was postponed twice for a more "sufficient gameplay examination.” That’s one way to get to play it early. After being initially pushed from October 2 to October 8, it was pushed once more and the committee met again on October 18. The second review passed a vote for an Adults Only rating with eight voting in favor of the rating and one voting against classification. The content descriptors were assigned as “Sensuality, Violence, Crime, Drugs, and Language.” That first one, “Sensuality,” was the issue. According to the report, the committee took particular issue with male nudity without any sexual context. The South Korean ratings board revised its regulation rules in September 2025, but previously even a suggestion of nudity could land a game with an Adults Only rating. After the revision, this wording changed to "cases where suggestive bodily exposure is directly and specifically depicted." GTA 6 was the first game to run into the new, apparently more relaxed, rules. No such rules exist for crime or drug depictions. A rating refusal would have blocked the release of GTA 6 in South Korea entirely. According to the report, the ratings board felt pressure with potentially being the sole country to refuse classification to the biggest game of the year. Last month, GTA 6 received an age rating of PEGI 18 , which included mentions of "decapitation," the ability for players to snort cocaine at any time, "scenes of sexual fetishes," and much more. The rating, since deleted, described GTA 6's violence as "bloody with a high degree of realism." Some weapons will be more brutal than others, with some said to be "able to cause greater damage, such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment." Rockstar has made drug use "frequent and prominent," with players able to partake in illicit substances. Cocaine is said to be especially important in Vice City, with the rating promising that Jason and Lucia will be able to use the substance directly from their inventory, as it can be "snorted directly from their hand at any time." The GTA 6 PEGI description also touched on " strong sexual themes ," which include "nudity, scenes of intercourse, and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes." None of this should come as much of a surprise, given the GTA 6 launch trailer teases steamy shower scenes between Jason and Lucia . Not long now: GTA 6 is out on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. IGN's latest coverage includes speculation about a potential beloved legacy character from a previous game hiding in the latest GTA 6 trailer , and the release of new GTA 6 footage that looks so real fans actually thought it was real-life . Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: GTA 6 Was Almost Refused Classification In South Korea For Featuring Too Many ‘Out-Of-Context’ Penises
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto IV GTA 6 Rockstar Games Take-Two Interactive Grand Theft Auto 6 came very close to being denied an age rating in South Korea, which would have effectively resulted in Rockstar Gamesâ release being banned in the country. But what could have possibly led the Game Content Rating Board to consider such a measure? Was it the drug use? Something gambling-related, maybe? Nope. In the words of GCRBâs committee members, it was because GTA 6 features too much âout-of-context genital nudityâ and a whole lot of âfrequent male genital exposure.â These quotes come directly from three separate GCRB reviews of GTA 6âs content, as outlined and translated in a report from Inven Global . According to Inven Global âs investigation, GCRBâs initial September 10 review ended in a tie, with three committee members voting in favor of refusing the game classification. Because the other three voters wished to classify GTA 6 as an âAdults Onlyâ title in South Korea (a 19+ rating), a second vote was held on October 2. However, the GCRBâs second vote was inconclusive, with committee members citing the lack of a fully playable build of GTA 6 as the reason. But by October 16, another vote took place, this time passing the game with an Adults Only rating by eight to one. Three more people showed up this time, it seems. And why did the mood change so much? It appears the previous rulings had been based on leaked footage showing Jason running around in the buff . O ne committee member, apparently after playing the official version of the game, stated that âit appears [Rockstar Games had] intentionally covered genital exposure in explicitly sexual scenes.â Inven Globalâs report specifically states that the GCRB was referring to âproblematic scenes featured in leaked overseas footageâ in this context. Considering thereâs only one high-profile GTA 6 leaker, this is presumably referencing Cyberleekâs videos published between August and October. More specifically, Cyberleek shared videos of Jason hanging dong and Lucia skydiving in the nude . However, the nudity in these clips was seemingly only made possible through the use of developer tools in the build of the game Cyberleek had acquired. It sounds like the GCRB was concerned that Jason and Lucia could strip down to their birthday suits in normal gameplay, and the committee members only chose to approve the Adults Only rating once they were able to confirm otherwise. This seems to indirectly imply that Jason cannot, in fact, hang dong in GTA 6 . Apologies in advance to the girls and gays. Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. sources.title: GTA 6 was almost refused classification in South Korea due to the sheer amount of genitals shown
sources.text: Also, the naked Jason seen in leaks seemingly isn't part of the final game GTA 6 was reportedly almost refused classification to release in South Korea, with the sheer amount of genitals being the sticking point for many. GTA 6 is almost guaranteed to get high age ratings from every ratings board. The series has historically received the highest ratings every time a new game releases, and as Rockstar continues to push that boundary and the fidelity of the acts in the games grows even more realistic, it's only natural that things will come under scrutiny from ratings boards. The European ratings board has already reported "detailed decapitation and dismemberment" as well as rampant drug use, while the Australian ratings board lists sex scenes. This has even raised concerns that the game will be censored in Japan due to its lack of certain disclaimers. Per Inven , GTA 6 reportedly came close to being refused by South Korea's Game Content Rating Board before it landed on an Adults Only rating. The big sticking point during these meetings was apparently due to frequent genital exposure "without context". We've already seen from leaks that the game will feature nudist beaches with all sorts on show. Over the course of three reviews by the ratings board, the decision had gone from a split vote, with three members each voting between adults-only and refused classification, to an eight-to-one vote in favor of an adults-only rating. Notably, it's mentioned that the leaked footage featuring Jason naked is not included in the final game. And that any sex scenes are only cutscenes rather than playable, like the infamous Hot Coffee incident of GTA San Andreas. GTA 6 won't run at 60fps even on PS5 Pro, but Sony's console does have an exclusive: ray-traced shadows and PSSR. 4. stories.summary: Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann has given a seemingly promising update on Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and offered a fresh tease of what to expect.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet in 'Last Stages of Production,' Neil Druckmann calls it a Mash-up of Jak and Daxter, Uncharted and The Last of Us
sources.text: Naughty Dog boss Neil Druckmann has given a seemingly promising update on the studio's long-awaited Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet , and offered a fresh tease of what to expect. PlayStation's upcoming, under-wraps space blockbuster remains largely a mystery, despite being revealed almost two years ago at The Game Awards in December 2024. We know only fragments of its story, and still have no idea when it will launch. Speaking at the Comic Creators Block Party 2026 , Druckmann said Intergalactic was now moving into its "last stages of production" and that the game was playable, with work now focusing on "refining and polishing." More intriguingly still, Druckmann described Intergalactic as an amalgamation of three other famous Naughty Dog franchises, with elements included from each. "We used to have another game franchise called Jak and Daxter," Druckmann began. "And with this one, we really wanted to take everything we learned from that franchise, which is sci-fi fantasy, the action-adventure stuff we learned with Uncharted, the more kind of serious drama we got for The Last of Us, and it really is a combination of those three franchises. "We wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems," he added. "Can we sustain the cinematic storytelling we're used to doing and go even deeper with gameplay systems?" From the little that's been revealed of Intergalactic so far, we know that it will be an alternate universe sci-fi tale starring a bounty hunter stranded on a distant planet in the far future. This bounty hunter is Jordan A. Mun, played by Tati Gabrielle, with her bounty targets played by a roster of famous faces including Tony Dalton, Kumail Nanjiani and Ashley Scott. Naughty Dog regular Troy Baker is also set to appear. Back in 2025, Intergalactic was reported to still be a couple of years from release , though PlayStation and Naughty Dog have refrained from narrowing its release window officially. That said, Druckmann recently indicated that the game would get a full unveiling at some point in the next 12 months . If it feels like a while since you've played something new from Naughty Dog, arguably PlayStation's most high-profile studio, you're not wrong. Naughty Dog's last all-new release was The Last of Us Part 2, which released back in 2020. The intervening years have seen the studio launch various remasters, and scrap a multiplayer The Last of Us spinoff after years of work. Intergalactic is just one of several projects in development at Naughty Dog, however, and fans now widely believe a new installment of Uncharted is also in the works . sources.text: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Naughty Dog Naughty Dog has been especially quiet onÂ Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet since its original announcement in late 2024. We learned in August of this year that mo-cap filming had wrapped, but even then the Last of Us studio was especially tight-lipped about when we might hear anything new about the sci-fi game. Rumors were there thatÂ IntergalacticÂ was aiming for a 2027 release, with unfortunate reports that Naughty Dog employees were being crunched yet again to achieve this, but it’s not until now that these rumors seem more concrete. Speaking to Patton Oswalt during an interview at Comic Creators Block Party 2026 (thanks PushSquare ), Druckmann revealed that the game is in the “last stage of production,” and is already fully playable. During a livestream from Revenge of TV on November 7, Patton Oswalt attempted to get Neil Druckmann to spill some new information about the forthcoming science-fiction bounty-hunting game, the first new IP from Naughty Dog in something like 300,000 years. Druckmann remained resolutely on-message, refusing to divulge any actual information about what happens in the game beyond naming the actors we already know are in it. “We’ve only teased it, so I can’t talk too much about it,” Druckmann told Oswalt, “but we’re kind of like at the last stages of production, where we can play it, and we’re refining it and polishing it, and I can’t wait to show it to the world.” Neil Druckmann habla sobre #Intergalactic ð ðï¸ "Estamos en la Ãºltima etapa de producciÃ³n" ðï¸ "Lo estamos perfeccionando y puliendo" ðï¸ "Es una combinaciÃ³n de las franquicias de Jak, Uncharted y TLOU". ðï¸ "EnseÃ±aremos GAMEPLAY e HISTORIA en 2027" pic.twitter.com/NPpqVHtUd2 — Intergalacticâ¢ ES (@IntergalacticES) November 11, 2026 “We’re going to show a lot next year,” Druckmann continued. “We’re gonna show gameplay, more of the story- I think we’re going to really surprise people with what they think the game is and what it actually is.” He then adds that the game “has a really big cast,” but that Naughty Dog wants people to learn who’s in the game by playing, rather than from earlier reveals. sources.title: Palworld Developer Pocketpair Gives Employees 5 Days Off to Play GTA 6
sources.text: Palworld developer Pocketpair is giving its staff five days off to make their way through GTA 6 . “All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA 6 launches,” the company said in a tweet . The company also shared a letter it presumably sent out internally to workers at the studio. “To all employees,” the letter started. “On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin. “At Pocketpair, we believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention. Therefore, after careful consideration, we have decided that all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto VI will be granted a special five-day holiday. The holiday period starts on GTA 6 launch date, November 19, and ends on November 23. “During this period, employees will be excused from their regular duties and are instead encouraged to take a business trip to Vice City,” the letter said. “We hope everyone enjoys their time away from the office and returns safely from their travels.” All Pocketpair employees have been granted special leave to attend to an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City when GTA6 launches. Please see the attached notice for details. https://t.co/qJjJ7IvhhY Pocketpair boss Takuro Mizobe tweeted to confirm he'll be making the most of the special holiday, saying: "Of course, I’ll be taking a break for a while to play GTA6 too!" Pocketpair isn’t the only company talking about GTA 6’s launch. The developer behind Wardogs encouraged its players to “go play GTA 6” and come back to the game after its next big update. Hardware company Logitech also announced that it will be giving employees time off for GTA 6 . According to a new report, GTA 6 has caused a 17% spike in people requesting time off work , so it’s probably for the best. Not long now! GTA 6 is out on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S. IGN's latest coverage includes speculation about a potential beloved legacy character from a previous game hiding in the latest GTA 6 trailer , and the release of new GTA 6 footage that looks so real fans actually thought it was real-life . sources.title: One Company Is Giving All Of Its 7,000 Employees The Day Off To Play GTA 6
sources.text: Logitech, rather than processing the no-doubt massive load of time-off requests that would all mysteriously happen to fall on the same day, is just declaring November 19th its Logi Game Day and letting everybody take it off. Why November 19th? Guess. Estimates put the company at just over 7,000 employees and all of them, from executives to interns, will get the day off to play GTA VI, any other game, or no game at all. It’s a day off, don’t let Logitech tell you what to do with it. No matter what its employees decide to do with their time, the company is smartly getting ahead of economists’ prognostications about just how much GTA VI will cost the economy in folks calling out of work to play by just dialing its productivity for the day down to zero. What’s especially funny is that the press release for the event frontloads a bunch of statistics that talk about how gaming is good for professional performance. “In the companyâs recent Logitech Ctrl Tomorrow study, 81% of gamers believe that gaming builds real-world confidence, reduces anxiety, and correlates with stronger day-to-day work performance.” Yes, these things are probably true. But let’s not pretend that saying “As a company designing products for work and play, we see every day how engagement in one sphere supports performance in the other” is anything but the corporate version of handing your gym teacher a forged note from your mom saying it’s okay to skip class, except your gym teacher in this case is Logitech shareholders and your mom is GTA VI . sources.title: Palworld devs get 5 days off to play GTA 6
sources.text: "We believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention" We're now one week away from the launch of GTA 6 , and Palworld studio Pocketpair has announced that it'll be giving devs excited to play Rockstar's game the time off to do so, because "we believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention." I don't know about you, but I suspect that November 19 may see a lot of people around the world calling in sick to their jobs thanks to a sudden bout of illness that's going to take them until at least after the weekend to recover from. Pocketpair might be anticipating that itself, as a staff notice also shared on Twitter confirms that they'll all be able to "undertake a business trip to Vice City," if they please. "On November 19, millions of gamers around the world will find themselves sitting at school or work, gazing longingly out the window, knowing that a new era of gaming is about to begin," the notice starts. "At Pocketpair, we believe that such a historic occasion deserves our full attention. "Therefore," it continues, "after careful consideration, we have decided that all employees who intend to play Grand Theft Auto VI will be granted a special five-day holiday." That period, of course, runs from November 19 to November 23, during which "employees will be excused from their regular duties and are instead encouraged to undertake a business trip to Vice City. We hope everyone enjoys their time away from the office and returns safely from their travels." I genuinely thought that this was a joke post at first, but separate tweets from Pocketpair CEO Takuro Mizobe and head of publishing John "Bucky" Buckley indicate otherwise. Mizobe says (via machine translation) that he'll be taking time off to play GTA 6 himself, while Bucky admits that "things might be a bit quiet" while the team is busy playing Rockstar's new title. Bucky previously joked that Slay the Spire 2's release had delayed Palworld's 1.0 launch by "at least a whole day" after Mizobe got a telling off for staying up all night to play it , and I'd imagine the company might want to avoid a similar situation here. Better than having everyone in the office getting no work done, right? Pocketpair wants to make it clear that the GTA 6 holiday won't affect any of its schedules, though: "Please note that update work for Palworld and Craftopia is proceeding smoothly and is expected to be carried out as scheduled," it adds. Let the devs have their fun, basically.
